summary: We developed mission 101, a web app designed to help astronauts keep track of their physical and mental health during space missions. Instead of juggling separate logs, the app brings everything into one dashboard with five main sections: Exercises (a workout timer and activity tracker), Wellbeing (daily mood tracking and journaling), Nutrition (weekly meal planning), Radiation log (tracking exposure against NASA career and single-event safety limits), and Environment (monitoring cabin temperature, pressure, and daily hygiene).   Spaceflight puts a massive strain on the human body—from muscle and bone loss in microgravity to vision changes, radiation exposure, and the stress of isolation. Our app addresses this challenge by giving crew members a simple, offline-ready tool to monitor their daily habits and catch warning signs early. It also includes quick, built-in info cards explaining why each habit matters in space. Keeping astronauts healthy is essential for any successful mission, and making self-monitoring effortless helps protect the crew on long-duration flights.
details: Rather than looking like a cold, intimidating medical terminal, we designed the interface with soft earth tones, smooth transitions, and custom animations—like a pedaling cyclist when the exercise timer runs—to keep daily check-ins approachable during stressful missions. We also built in practical safeguards based on real human factors: full undo/redo controls .
